title: Reduce storage and host-class uncertainty before implementation
description:
## Purpose

Buy down the uncertainty in `chatticus-fbae4e` by trying things for real, before any implementation is authorized.

This epic is **experiments and cheap fact-checks only**. Nothing here builds product code. Each child states the question it answers, what would falsify the current design, and what it costs to run.

## Why this ordering

Working out what each unknown actually gates produced a result worth recording, because it is not the order the initiative's own narrative suggests:

| Piece of the design | Needs tunnel? | Needs WAN NFS? | Value | Gated by an experiment here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EFS for AWS hosts (delete lease, snapshot, hydrate) | No | No | High — large deletion | **None.** No unknowns block it. |
| Accelerated batch (GPU on owned hardware) | No | No | Highest — $100s–$1000s per run | Long-running job spike |
| Local *interactive* host (Antharchy GUI) | Yes | Yes | Lowest — ~$30–60/mo | NFS-over-WAN spike |

**The WAN metadata question — flagged in the initiative as "load-bearing and unmeasured" — gates only the least valuable piece.** The EFS simplification for AWS hosts has no WAN dependency, and accelerated batch needs neither EFS nor a tunnel. That makes the NFS spike safe to defer and the long-running-job spike the one to run first.

## Ordering

1. **Long-running job spike** — gates the highest-value host class, independent of everything else.
2. **Cheap fact-checks** (Fargate capabilities, turn concurrency) — minutes each, no spike required.
3. **NFS-over-WAN spike** — run before committing engineering time to the local interactive host, not before the two tracks that do not depend on it.

## Not experiments

Recorded here so nobody spends a spike on them: AWS pricing (look it up), and reverse SSH tunnelling from behind home NAT (thoroughly established; latency is worth knowing eventually but would not change the design).

## Status 2026-09-05

Campaign ran against the live Anthus account. See the learnings comment on this epic and on each child.

- `0edb18` **closed** — multi-day training is not a turn; D8 corrected.
- `0b10d6` **closed** — Fargate cannot host WireGuard; D2 verified.
- `766c51` **closed** — one bot can have concurrent turns; workspace_id is the isolation boundary.
- `9af381` **open / parked** — Phase A blocked: no Chatticus EFS. Phase B waits on CDK.

- `ea918a` **open** — added on review. D5's long-`actimeo` mitigation rests on a premise `766c51` falsified. A decision, not an experiment.

EFS-for-AWS-hosts is not gated by remaining *experiments* here. It is touched by `ea918a`, which applies at default `actimeo` whenever concurrent turns for one bot land on different hosts. Local interactive host remains gated by both `9af381` and `ea918a`.

comments.text:
## Learnings (2026-09-05 campaign)

Tried in the live Anthus account (`335163751677`, `us-east-1`). Nothing here authorizes product implementation.

| Child | Question | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `0edb18` | Can a multi-day training run be a turn? | **No.** Turn failed ~4.5 min into a 30 min job. Accelerated batch needs a manifold **job kind**, not a longer timeout. Corrects `fbae4e` D8. |
| `0b10d6` | Can Fargate host a WireGuard peer? | **No.** Docs and live `RegisterTaskDefinition`: `ClientException: NET_ADMIN is not allowed on Fargate`. D2 stands; verify caveat removed. |
| `766c51` | Can one bot have two turns in flight? | **Yes.** No bot-level mutex. `workspace_id` is the isolation boundary, not "one turn per bot." |
| `9af381` | Is NFS-over-WAN usable for a hot tree? | **Not measurable yet.** No Chatticus EFS, mount targets, or tunnel EC2. Phase A blocked with a diagnosed cause. Did not touch Kanbus EFS `fs-09fcbd58a2e2d2c98`. |

### What this unblocks

- **EFS for AWS hosts** (delete lease / snapshot / hydrate) was never gated by these experiments. Still true.
- **Accelerated batch** is unblocked as a *design* (job kind), blocked as *implementation* until that kind exists. Do not stretch `turn_deadline` or `CHATTICUS_HOST_WORKER_SECONDS`.
- **Local interactive host** remains gated on CDK EFS + tunnel, then Phase B of `9af381`.

### What would be the wrong next step

- Building a Fargate WireGuard endpoint.
- Treating a long GPU run as a turn with bigger timeouts.
- Mounting the Kanbus filesystem to "just get NFS numbers."
- Implementing the local interactive host before a Chatticus EFS exists.

comments.text:
## New item from reviewing the campaign (2026-09-05)

`chatticus-ea918a` — **the actimeo vs concurrent-workspace contradiction.** Answering `766c51` falsified the premise D5 was resting on. D5 calls a long `actimeo` its load-bearing mitigation and justifies it by single-writer-per-workspace scoping; `766c51` established turns are not serialized per bot and the default is one workspace per bot. Concurrent readers of a shared workspace are therefore the default case.

"NFS arbitrates concurrent writers" does not answer it — the failure mode is attribute-cache **staleness**, not corruption, and close-to-open consistency does not apply because `git status` calls `lstat()` rather than `open()`.

**This is not gated behind `9af381`.** The epic records EFS-for-AWS-hosts as having no unknowns blocking it. That remains true of experiments, but AWS hosts have the same exposure at default `actimeo` — a smaller window, still nonzero — whenever concurrent turns for one bot land on different hosts. Two turns on one NFS client are coherent; different hosts are not.

D5 and D3 on `fbae4e` have been corrected to stop asserting the falsified premise. D3's "the two-writer problem stops existing" now carries a qualification: true for write arbitration, not for cache coherence.

Also added **Phase A0** to `9af381` — a netem pre-experiment answering the D5 threshold question with no AWS, tunnel, or CDK, which also produces the staleness curve `ea918a` needs.
